WITH filtered_returns AS (
    SELECT
        sr.sr_ticket_number,
        sr.sr_item_sk,
        sr.sr_customer_sk,
        sr.sr_returned_date_sk
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN date_dim d2
      ON d2.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
    WHERE d2.d_year = 2001
      AND d2.d_moy = 8
),
sales_with_diff AS (
    SELECT
        ss.ss_store_sk,
        fr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk AS diff
    FROM filtered_returns fr
    JOIN store_sales ss
      ON ss.ss_ticket_number = fr.sr_ticket_number
     AND ss.ss_item_sk = fr.sr_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d1
      ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk = fr.sr_customer_sk
),
bucketed AS (
    SELECT
        ss_store_sk,
        CASE
            WHEN diff IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN diff <= 30 THEN 0
            WHEN diff <= 60 THEN 1
            WHEN diff <= 90 THEN 2
            WHEN diff <= 120 THEN 3
            ELSE 4
        END AS bucket
    FROM sales_with_diff
),
bucket_counts AS (
    SELECT
        ss_store_sk,
        bucket,
        COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM bucketed
    GROUP BY ss_store_sk, bucket
),
pivoted AS (
    SELECT
        ss_store_sk,
        SUM(CASE WHEN bucket = 0 THEN cnt ELSE 0 END) AS "30 days",
        SUM(CASE WHEN bucket = 1 THEN cnt ELSE 0 END) AS "31-60 days",
        SUM(CASE WHEN bucket = 2 THEN cnt ELSE 0 END) AS "61-90 days",
        SUM(CASE WHEN bucket = 3 THEN cnt ELSE 0 END) AS "91-120 days",
        SUM(CASE WHEN bucket = 4 THEN cnt ELSE 0 END) AS ">120 days"
    FROM bucket_counts
    GROUP BY ss_store_sk
)
SELECT
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip,
    SUM(p."30 days")::bigint AS "30 days",
    SUM(p."31-60 days")::bigint AS "31-60 days",
    SUM(p."61-90 days")::bigint AS "61-90 days",
    SUM(p."91-120 days")::bigint AS "91-120 days",
    SUM(p.">120 days")::bigint AS ">120 days"
FROM pivoted p
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_store_sk = p.ss_store_sk
GROUP BY
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip
ORDER BY
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip
LIMIT 100

1. TWO-PHASE AGGREGATION — TARGET: the ten-column `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY` on `s_store_name, s_company_id, s_street_number, s_street_name, s_street_type, s_suite_number, s_city, s_county, s_state, s_zip` over the joined `store_sales`/`store_returns` rows — TRANSFORMATION: first aggregate the filtered join by `ss_store_sk` (one integer) into per-store bucket counts, then join that ≤44-row result to `store` and re-aggregate by the original ten attributes; this turns the expensive row-level hash/sort on ten wide string columns into an integer-key aggregation plus a trivial final rollup, while preserving duplicate-attribute grouping exactly.

2. BUCKET-AND-PIVOT PREAGGREGATION — TARGET: the five repeated `sum(case when sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk ... end)` expressions — TRANSFORMATION: in the per-`ss_store_sk` aggregation, evaluate the day difference once, assign a single 0..4 bucket, and `count(*)` per `(ss_store_sk, bucket)`; afterward pivot the ≤220 bucket counts into the five named output columns, removing four of the five per-row CASE evaluations and all repeated subtraction.

3. COVERING INDEX FOR THE RETURN→SALE PROBE — TARGET: `store_sales.ss_ticket_number/ss_item_sk` PK lookup from `store_returns`, plus heap columns `ss_customer_sk`, `ss_sold_date_sk`, `ss_store_sk` — TRANSFORMATION: add a covering index on `store_sales(ss_ticket_number, ss_item_sk) INCLUDE (ss_customer_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_store_sk)` so the return-driven lookup is index-only and avoids heap accesses into the 57.6M-row `store_sales` table.

4. JOIN-PREDICATE DECOMPOSITION — TARGET: the three-column equality `ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number AND ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk AND ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk` — TRANSFORMATION: match `store_returns` to `store_sales` first on the two-column unique key `(ticket_number, item_sk)`, then apply `ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk` as a residual filter after the unique probe; this keeps the join one-to-one and lets the planner use the `store_sales` primary key for an index nested-loop join instead of hashing both large tables on three columns.
